Form 1-SU — startup disclosure statement (proposed form) [member]

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. The Rule 103 information an issuer relying on the startup exemption must make publicly accessible at the website named in its Form NOR, and any amendment made within 30 days after a calendar year-end because of material changes. Auditchain Labs recommends (Request for Comment 65) that this disclosure be an official form, Form 1-SU, filed with the Commission in structured form (XBRL) in the same way an offering statement is filed, signed like Form 1-CRYPTO, and posted on the issuer's website in Inline XBRL, so that the Commission can capture every fact of every filing in the lifecycle of a project and supervise in an automated manner.

Covered transactions [abstract]

Ledger of every covered transaction under the startup exemption: capital-raising sales, distributions including airdrops, and rewards or incentives for operating, governing or securing the network or application. The ledger is what the $5,000,000 limit and the four-year window are tested against.

Units of covered investment contracts offered

Number of units of covered investment contract offered, in the unit the issuer defines. Rule 101(e)(1) as proposed makes one unit of a covered investment contract one unit of the subject crypto asset; Auditchain Labs recommends that an issuer be permitted to define the unit as a functional unit - the subject crypto asset together with the software or other technical primitives the crypto asset invokes (for Pacioli.ai, a Pacioli Validating Node of 50,000 AUDT with its node software license) - with the Rule 101(e) measures reported alongside in the functional-unit elements. Where the unit is the crypto asset itself, the two agree.

Price per unit of the covered investment contract, in the unit the issuer defines (see UnitsOfCoveredInvestmentContractsOffered). Rule 101(e)(2) as proposed determines it by reference to the price per unit of the subject crypto asset; that measure is reported in EquivalentPurchasePricePerUnitOfSubjectCryptoAsset. Functional unit of covered investment contract and Rule 101(e) equivalents [abstract]

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Auditchain Labs recommends (Requests for Comment 6, 7 and 31) that an issuer may define the unit of a covered investment contract as a functional unit: the subject crypto asset together with the software or other technical primitives the crypto asset invokes and that an institution needs to stand up and operate the network (for Pacioli.ai, a Pacioli Validating Node of 50,000 AUDT with its node software license). The elements below carry the crypto-asset content of each unit and the measures Rule 101(e) as proposed would report, so the Commission can read the offering either way and the per-crypto-asset arithmetic can be checked. The recommendation is intended to make the exemption easier to use for building real utility than for a token sale with nothing behind it.

Disagreements with the former accountant

True if, during the two most recent fiscal years and any later interim period before the resignation, declination or dismissal, there was any disagreement with the former accountant on accounting principles or practices, financial statement disclosure, or auditing scope or procedure that, if not resolved to its satisfaction, would have caused it to refer to the matter in its report. Includes disagreements later resolved; a difference of opinion is enough, and an oral communication from the engagement partner generally suffices (Item 304(a)(1)(iv); Instructions 4-5).

Describes each disagreement (Item 304(a)(1)(iv)(A)).

True if the issuer has authorized the former accountant to respond fully to the successor accountant's inquiries on the subject matter of each disagreement or reportable event (Item 304(a)(1)(iv)(C), (v)).

Reportable events

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. The merkle root of this filing, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, computed by the method reported in the filing over every fact in the filing except this root, the method and the facts in the table of anchors. It is recorded on a blockchain network before the filing is filed; the table of anchors gives the record.
Method used to compute the merkle root of the filing
Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. The method used to compute the merkle root of the filing.
Merkle root method [domain]
Reg CA filing merkle tree, version 1 [member]

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Each fact is written as a JSON object with the keys concept, entity, period, dimensions, unit, decimals and value, leaving out keys with no value; concepts, dimensions and members are written as namespace, "#" and local name, and a typed dimension by its value. The object is serialized under RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme). Each leaf is SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of the byte 0x00 followed by that serialization; the leaves are sorted in ascending order and combined into the Merkle Tree Hash of RFC 6962, section 2.1. Left out of the root: the root itself, this method and every fact in the table of anchors.
